sources.claim: Deductions reduce taxable income; credits reduce tax dollar for dollar; refundable credits can produce a refund beyond tax owed (for example, the Earned Income Tax Credit).

sections.skill: Compare the value of tax deductions and tax credits, including refundable credits

questions.prompt: Omar's marginal tax rate is 12%. Which saves him more tax: a $1,000 deduction or a $1,000 credit?
questions.intro: A deduction lowers taxable income, so it saves tax equal to the deduction × your marginal rate. A credit lowers the tax itself, dollar for dollar.
sources: IRS (Credits and deductions for individuals): Deductions reduce taxable income; credits reduce tax dollar for dollar; refundable credits can produce a refund beyond tax owed (for example, the Earned Income Tax Credit). (https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions-for-individuals)

questions.prompt: Omar's tax before credits is $4,560. He qualifies for a $1,500 credit. What is his tax after the credit?
questions.intro: Tax after credits = tax before credits − credits.

misconceptions.C: Treats the credit like a deduction at 12%

questions.prompt: Tia's tax before credits is $300. She qualifies for a $1,000 NONREFUNDABLE credit. What is her tax after the credit?

choices.text: −$700, paid to her as a refund

questions.intro: A nonrefundable credit can reduce your tax to zero but not below. A refundable credit can reduce tax below zero, and the extra is paid to you as a refund.
questions.feedback: A nonrefundable credit stops at $0; the unused $700 is lost.
sources: IRS (Credits and deductions for individuals): Deductions reduce taxable income; credits reduce tax dollar for dollar; refundable credits can produce a refund beyond tax owed (for example, the Earned Income Tax Credit). (https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions-for-individuals)

questions.prompt: Tia owes $300 of tax before credits and qualifies for a $1,000 REFUNDABLE credit. What happens?

choices.text: Her tax becomes $0 and the extra $700 is lost
Nothing, because refundable credits need $1,000 of tax
Her tax becomes $0 and she receives $700 more

questions.correct_answer: Her tax becomes $0 and she receives $700 more
questions.intro: Refundable credits are paid out even when they exceed the tax owed.
questions.feedback: $300 − $1,000 = −$700, paid to her (plus any withholding refund).
sources: IRS (Credits and deductions for individuals): Deductions reduce taxable income; credits reduce tax dollar for dollar; refundable credits can produce a refund beyond tax owed (for example, the Earned Income Tax Credit). (https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions-for-individuals)

questions.prompt: Which credit is designed for low- to moderate-income workers and is refundable?
questions.intro: The Earned Income Tax Credit helps low- to moderate-income workers, especially families with children. It is refundable, so it can result in a refund even if no tax is owed. Many eligible workers do not claim it.
questions.feedback: The EITC is a refundable credit for working people with lower incomes.
sources: IRS (Credits and deductions for individuals): Deductions reduce taxable income; credits reduce tax dollar for dollar; refundable credits can produce a refund beyond tax owed (for example, the Earned Income Tax Credit). (https://www.irs.gov/credits-deductions-for-individuals)
